newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close sharply higher.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates finished sharply higher on Friday amid tight liquidity after the central bank's recent squeeze of the already tight money situation in the banking system, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate surged to close at 7.544 percent, the highest level since February 26, against Thursday's already high 7.001 close -- far outside of the central bank's 5.00-5.5 percent target zone.
The 30-day commercial paper ended at 7.5 against 7.00-7.25.
Dealers said big banks were pessimistic about the banking system's liquidity, adding the central bank's attitude would determine next week's movements.

The central bank launched big issues of negotiable certificates of deposit on Wednesday and Thursday to mop up funds in the banking system, fuelling suspicions that it was trying to take some of the fire from the sizzling stock market.

Despite the central bank's consistent denials, analysts suspect its repeated issuance of the short-term instruments in recent weeks was an effort to draw liquidity away from the stock market, which has surged 25 percent in 1997 alone on increasingly huge turnover.
Dealers said they did not rule out the possibility of further NCD issue by the central bank as some T$36 billion of earlier NCDs were due to mature next week.
The bond market is expected to enter a consolidation phase next week. The benchmark 10-year 86/4 government bond was trading at a yield of 6.0925-0930 percent in earlier session.
